summary: A public walkthrough of producing a verifiable receipt with runx, written from a run that actually happened and was re-verified afterwards: the two-file skill layout, the content-addressed receipt the run leaves, and how to read a verify verdict, including the difference between a valid local-development signature and a third-party attestation. The page is original, describes what runx is, and links runx.ai and github.com/runxhq/runx in its body text.
audience: developers and agent-tool authors who need to show what an automated run did, and reviewers who have to decide whether a receipt is worth trusting
venue: own project site (validator-community.com), a registered project domain; no venue rule restricts describing or linking runx here
why_allowed: The page is on my own project domain, not a community that disallows project sharing, and it is editorial content rather than a comment, profile, or signature. It adds reader value independently of the link: the receipt-anatomy and signature-mode sections explain something the tool's own examples do not state plainly, so the link is a consequence of the writing rather than its purpose.
why_allowed_in_venue: Own registered project domain; describing and linking a tool I used is on-topic for a delivery-practice section, and no third-party venue rules are involved.

observations.label: what the page contributes
observations.value: Receipt anatomy (which fields a verifier should read first), the three separate verification checks, and the signature-mode distinction
observations.note: The honest section is the load-bearing one: status=valid together with mode=local-development is a self-consistency claim, not a third-party attestation, and a verifier that treats them as equal overstates what it verified
